notes: Main disagreements: (1) policy_type between neighbouring types (P15/P32 for AI as input, P24/P27 for crediting, P35/P40 for process requirements, P01/P06 for default bans, P04/P63 for sample-policy support), resolved by re-reading the sentence and choosing the type whose definition it states without inferring unstated purposes; (2) modality, mostly should/must for teaching-center advice and informs/must-not for statements that classify an act as misconduct, resolved by whether the sentence is an imperative; (3) actor/phase for AI-assisted grading principles, set to instructor/during-work consistently; (4) one document stance (university guidelines: A permit, B delegates), resolved as permit because the page attaches conditions and never hands the decision to instructors; (5) A split three grading principles that B merged, kept as separate rules. Only-one-coder units were all real policy statements and kept, except one B cross-reference ('See the Honor Council statement') which was dropped as navigation. Matching was by anchor position and rule.
